headline: The United States imported nearly twice as many chips in the first eight months of 2026 as a year earlier, as AI data-center building pulled in foreign supply.
score_reason: Curator score 5 lowered by 1: the trade data was released on 6 Oct 2026, before the 10 Oct start of today's window; the Yahoo Finance analysis itself is from 10 Oct.
importance_line: The US is buying far more foreign-made chips than a year ago, which matters to American buyers and policymakers and to chipmakers abroad, though the imports also reflect strong business spending on AI.
summary: Yahoo Finance reports, using new Commerce Department trade data, that the US imported nearly $90.5 billion of chips in the first eight months of 2026 against $49.2 billion a year earlier, while exports rose by more than $10 billion but were far outpaced by demand. In August alone the US ran a chip trade deficit of about $7.6 billion, compared with a small surplus of almost $400 million in August 2025, which Oxford Economics economist Grace Zwemmer links to business spending on AI hardware that she says shows no sign of slowing.
notes: Read in full via fulltext. Yahoo Finance's own reporting (byline Ben Werschkul), so it is the source. The underlying US trade data came out on 6 Oct 2026 (found in Census, Reuters, CNBC and Yahoo Finance items of that date). The article prints the August import figure as '$15.4' without 'billion'; the summary uses only the stated deficit of $7.6 billion.
